quickfire.question: To build an expression tree from a postfix expression, when you encounter an operator you:
options: Push it onto the stack immediately
Pop two operand trees, make them children of a new operator node, push result
Pop one tree, make it the right child of the operator
Clear the stack and start a new subtree
quickfire.answer: Pop two operand trees, make them children of a new operator node, push result

fullTrace.questionText: Construct the expression tree for: a + b * c − d / e ^ f % g (direct Part-B Q4 from exam bank). Show the step-by-step algorithm — convert to postfix first, then build the tree using a stack.

steps.operation: Parse: a + b * c − d / e ^ f % g

steps.note: Result: a b c * + d e f ^ / g % -. (Apply operator-precedence algorithm with a stack)
Create leaf node 'a', push onto stack.
Pop c (right) and b (left). Create '*' node with b left, c right. Push subtree.
Pop *-subtree (right) and a (left). Create '+' node. Push.
Push leaf nodes d, e, f.
Pop f (right), e (left). Create '^' node. Push.
Root is '-'. Left subtree: a + (b*c). Right subtree: (d / e^f) % g.
